title: SPEC-0002 P4c: the engine's MIDI clock, ABI 2, and the page's clock path
by: metronome + forge (one session, two commits, hats marked in the prefixes)
zone: Metronome hat: crates/octocore/ (src/types.rs, domain.rs, engine.rs, lib.rs, tests/clock.rs), journal/metronome/. Conductor hat: adr/0009 amendment 1. Referee hat: harness/baseline.txt. No contract, golden hash, octoffi or octorun change

spec_rev: SPEC-0002 r1; p4-plan r1 accepted ('Accept p4', 2026-10-02 10:54 Paris); ADR-0009 proposed (#29) with amendment 1 in this pull request
artifact: pull request P4c, branch metronome/p4c-engine-clock, built on forge/p4b-two-ports-and-input (#30) and carrying its commits, P4a's and the plan's (merge #27, #29, #30, then this)

handoffs/evidence/p4c-abi2-red.txt and p4c-page-red.txt: the web module's native tests against inert stubs (12 failing, 3 passing by construction) and the page's Node tests against the P4b module and sources (17 failing, 3 passing by construction)

cargo xtask verify --base origin/main: 4 pass, 0 fail, 6 not_implemented; assertions 503 (baseline 462, 42 added, 1 removed under ADR-0009: abi::the_module_reports_abi_version_one, replaced by ..._two). apps/web: 178 Node tests (152 before), 40 Chromium tests (37 before), tsc --noEmit clean

Pulse positions: crates/octocore/tests/clock.rs pins every pulse's sample at 40, 120 and 240 BPM and 44.1 and 48 kHz (dyadic samples-per-tick pairs) over block sizes 1, 64, 128, 480 and 1000; 24 pulses are one quarter note; the same pulses come out of the module byte for byte (apps/web/engine/tests/abi_clock.rs) and reach two devices at 20.833 ms apart through the real AudioWorklet in Chromium (apps/web/test/browser/host.browser.test.ts)

ADR-0009 amendment 1: seven places the code differs from the ADR text, found by building it red first. The one that matters for a receiver: the first note sounds 11 ticks after Start (tests/conformance/AMBIGUITIES.md, 'the first note after Play'), which the ADR had called the same sample
unresolved: D0, the tick length (WENGE-0012), is still open. M3 (a step is a whole number of pulses) is an ignored test that names it. With amendment 1 item 3 there are two reasons a pattern is not on a receiver's grid: the 1.5 pulses a step is today, and the 11-tick offset of the first note. Owner: @beaudesign

ADR-0009 amendment 1 departs from decisions 2 and 4 in seven places, flagged for the owner: Start or Continue by the sequencer's position; pulses on the global grid; the clock turned on mid-run says where the sequencer is and turned off sends nothing; tick_position is the audio's place; overflow is dropped and counted; Reset while running sends Stop. Owner: @beaudesign may reject any before P4d builds on them
Nothing in the page turns the clock on yet; the clock-state control arrives with the follower in P4d, which also finishes M7 and M8. Owner: @beaudesign (accepts the smaller P4c)
What a real receiver does with this clock is not measured: S1 on a real port, then S3. No MIDI backend here. Owner: @beaudesign
The scheduler sends the clock to every chosen device (ADR-0009 decision 3). A per-port choice is a P4d question
The Node and Chromium tests are still not floored by name in the baseline (Referee request open). Owner: referee
